We welcome you to the Youth Commission meeting.

If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and give it
to the secretary. The maximum time for addressing the Commission is five minutes. If you wish to
address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will be heard during
the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Commission on a subject which
does not appear on the agenda but related to recreation or community service, you may make your
presentation under agenda item VII. Please be advised that the Commission cannot, under the State of
California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, take action on any item that does not appear on the agenda.

When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please make your
statement as brief as possible. Thank you.

Minutes
  Alhambra Youth Commission
  February 10, 2026

Call to Order
The Alhambra Youth Commission was called to order at 6:03 PM on February 10, 2026, at the Alhambra Civic Center
Library, 101 South 1st Street, Alhambra, CA 91801.

I. Roll Call
Commissioners Present: Leslie Chu, Pamela Ghazale, Arabella Hernandez, Isabella Hernandez,
Katherine Quintana, Suki Li
Staff Present: Brie Houghton (Deputy Director), Rosalyn Rojas (Recreation Supervisor).
Absent: Chen Yu Wang, Brendon Wu, Lydia Chen, Natalia Rosales

I. Flag Salute
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited with all members standing and participating.

III. Approval of Minutes (August 12, 2025 Meeting)
Motion to approve the minutes was made by Isabella Hernandez and seconded by Arabella Hernandez. Motion passed by
roll call vote.

IV. Staff Report

  A. Review of Recent Events

  Fiesta Alhambra (September 2025):
  Youth Commissioners volunteered in the family activity area, assisting with children’s games and
  activities. Staff acknowledged Natalia Rosales, Arabella Hernandez, and Isabella Hernandez for their
  participation.

  Pumpkin Run (October 2025):
  Limited commissioner participation occurred due to waiver requirements and scheduling challenges.
  Natalia and two additional commissioners assisted with children’s activities.

  Spark of Love Toy Drive (December 2025):
  The commission experienced a loss of momentum due to quorum and meeting cancellations in October
  and November. Donation boxes were successfully coordinated with the Fire Department; however,
  commissioners were unable to complete the planned donation delivery and photo opportunity.

  B. Attendance and Commission Challenges
  Staff reported that the primary challenge for the Youth Commission continues to be consistent attendance and
  coordination. Meetings are held once per month for approximately one hour (typically 30 minutes in practice),
  and while commissioners have many ideas, implementation has been difficult due to scheduling and quorum
  issues.

  C. Strategic Planning and Goal Setting
  Staff provided guidance on establishing realistic timelines, noting that projects may require multiple months of
  planning given the commission’s meeting schedule. Commissioners were encouraged to communicate between
  meetings and plan projects well in advance, particularly around seasonal breaks.
   D. New Business

  Youth Commission Independent Project Proposal
  Commissioners discussed initiating original Youth Commission-led activities to establish an independent
  identity and increase community visibility, rather than solely assisting with City events.

  Summer Camp Collaboration Proposal
  Staff proposed that the Youth Commission lead an activity during the City’s summer camp program in
  early June. The camp serves approximately 60 children and includes literacy and environmental
  programming.

    Commissioners discussed potential formats, including: crafts, games and competitions, field day-
  style activities, and educational presentations with interactive components

  Environmental Education Themes
  Commissioners expressed interest in environmental education topics such as: Climate change awareness,
  California wildfire prevention, and natural disaster preparedness. The group emphasized interactive,
  hands-on activities rather than traditional lectures.

  E. Action Items / Next Steps

    Staff, Rosalyn Rojas, will email camp themes and dates to commissioners.
    Staff will confirm Spark of Love deadlines and Fire Department coordination.
    Staff provide logos, flyer specs, and social media guidance.
    Staff will follow up on volunteer coordination for upcoming events.

V. Oral Communications
No additional public oral communications were presented.

VI. Commission Orals

    Commissioner Katherine Quintana expressed interest in participating in “Hello Neighbor” and other community
  engagement programs.
    President Pamela Ghazale expressed a desire to initiate an original community project to increase Youth
  Commission visibility and create a lasting legacy, rather than participating in pre-existing projects, which makes
  the commission look more like volunteers.
   Staff member Brie Houghton suggested incorporating the community project into Alhambra’s
  Summer Camp Program (Camp Alhambra 2026). The Commission could decide on themes,
  crafts, and other activities for the week or for specific days.
    President Pamela Ghazale emphasized the commission should be more hands-on. Suggesting a field day with
  children at the camp with interactive activities, which include prizes, to create everlasting impressions with the
  youth.
    President Pamela Ghazale and Commissioner Leslie Chu highlight the importance of improving communication
  among commissioners outside of scheduled meeting dates (e.g., email or text groups).
   Staff member Rosalyn Rojas also agreed and stated she will communicate with commissioners
  more frequently to brainstorm projects and ideas before Youth Commission meetings.
    Commissioner Suki Li suggested taking a more proactive approach by jumping into activities rather than spending
  excessive time planning during meetings, as overplanning may lead to overthinking and decreased participation.

VII. Adjournment

Staff, Brie Houghton calls the meeting to adjourn at 6:33 PM.
